question.question: When one instance is held committed at three replicas with different committed commands for it, does applying each record through the executor leave the same effect for the instance's key, or do the replicas' state machines end up holding different effects for the same instance?
question.importance: Execution is where a committed decision becomes observable state, so an instance that is committed with different commands at different replicas produces different effects for the same key: replicas then serve different values and can never reconcile without rewriting applied state. This is the applied form of the agreement concern and is stated as its own obligation because the adopted-vector claim excludes execution.
contexts: one instance committed at three replicas
the recoverer's NOOP vector against the peer's PUT vector produced by the recovery confirmed under claim C1
event_paths: each replica holds the instance COMMITTED (recoverer and third replica NOOP, peer PUT)
the harness applies each record with Exec.executeCommand and probes the instance's key
the three applied values are compared

question.trigger_rationale: This is the consumption side of the decision the resolution produces: B11-prepare-resolution carries the attributed cross-activity effect that the recovered value re-enters the normal accept and commit path (A1), and execution then derives the applied effect from that committed vector. The claim is stated separately from C1 because C1's accepted scope excludes execution, and the property is observed with the real executor and state application.

obligation.description: When several replicas each hold the same instance committed and each applies it to its own copy of the state machine, the effect they apply for the instance's key must be the same, because the applied effect is determined by the committed command vector of that instance.

scope.description: One instance held committed at three replicas on the captured snapshot, each applied through Exec.executeCommand with a GET probe reading the instance's key from the replicated store.
assumptions: each replica's record for the instance is COMMITTED and its dependencies are already satisfied locally
the key is the one the committed commands touch
excluded: the production executeCommands loop, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout
the history that produced each committed record

grounding.derivation: Execution consumes the committed vector: strongconnect applies the commands of each instance in the strongly connected component and marks them EXECUTED, and state.Command.Execute turns those commands into store effects. Two replicas that hold different committed commands for the same instance therefore apply different effects for the same key, which is the agreement property this claim fixes, independently of how the records came to differ.
grounding.applicability: Applies on the captured snapshot to any instance held committed at more than one replica, including a recovery that committed a NOOP vector for an instance another replica holds with a real command.
unresolved: the harness applies records directly rather than through the production execution loop, so scheduling and watermarks are not covered
alternatives: an alternative reading is that execution is out of scope for an obligation about adopting a value, which is exactly why this is recorded as its own claim rather than as part of C1

associations.rationale: The applied effect is produced here: the commands of the committed record are executed against the replica's store, so two different committed commands for one instance produce two different effects.

bindings.description: Execution entry for one committed instance: it checks the committed status, computes the strongly connected component and applies the component's commands.
